## Message for prospective students

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
**I'm not recruiting new graduate students at the moment.** The lab is
currently at capacity for both Master's and PhD supervision. This page
will be updated whenever new positions become available.
:::

**Undergraduate students at UFMS** interested in scientific initiation
(PIBIC/PIVIC) or a monograph project are still welcome to get in touch
— please send me an email (`diogo.provete[at]ufms.br`) with a brief
note about yourself, your research interests, and your goals.

I'm always happy to talk to people about ecology, evolution, and
science in general — even if there's no formal position open.

When positions do open, I can supervise graduate students in the
[Ecology and Conservation graduate program](https://ppgec.ufms.br) and
in Animal Biology at UFMS — check their websites for deadlines and
admission details.

### Recommended reading

- [Marco Mello — convencendo o orientador](https://marcoarmello.wordpress.com/2015/08/12/convencendoorientador/)
  (highly recommended, especially for undergraduates thinking about
  approaching a potential advisor — in Portuguese)
- [Fifteen questions to ask before attending grad school](https://esajournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/bes2.70047)
- [What to bring to a meeting with your advisor](http://www.avasthilab.org/2017/03/14/what-to-bring-to-a-meeting-with-your-advisor/)
- [Dicas para quem deseja ingressar na carreira acadêmica ainda na graduação](https://esajournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/bes2.1745)

## Available resources

Our lab has access to several facilities at INBIO (UFMS):

- **Field station in the Pantanal** — [Base de Estudos do Pantanal](https://propp.ufms.br/coordenadorias/base-de-estudos-do-pantanal/)
- **Multi-user molecular biology and image labs** —
  [stereomicroscope, light microscope, and SEM](https://ppgec.ufms.br/facilidadeslaboratorios/)
- **Natural history collections** — [Zoology](https://ccbs.ufms.br/colecao-zoologica/)
  and [Herbarium](https://ccbs.ufms.br/herbariocgms/), with several hundred
  catalogued specimens
- **LTER study site** at the Bodoquena Plateau —
  [PELD Bodoquena](http://peldbodoquena.wixsite.com/home)
- **High-performance computing cluster** at the
  [School of Computer Science](https://lscad.facom.ufms.br/~wiki/index.php/Home)

## Our core values

A research program in community ecology
([Werner 1998](https://academic.oup.com/book/51110/chapter-abstract/421887314))
should rest on three pillars:

1. **Quantitative natural history** ([Futuyma 1998](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/abs/10.1086/286097);
   [Underwood et al. 2000](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0022098100001817))
2. **Field and/or laboratory experimentation** (Underwood 1990;
   [1991](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-the-marine-biological-association-of-the-united-kingdom/article/abs/logic-of-ecological-experiments-a-case-history-from-studies-of-the-distribution-of-macroalgae-on-rocky-intertidal-shores/35E1B7A604216BCC17DD9A249ED352A9))
3. **Modelling** ([Levins 1966](https://www.jstor.org/stable/27836590))

Field observations reveal patterns (Levin 1978;
[1992](https://esajournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.2307/1941447)),
but only experiments uncover the [mechanisms](http://plato.stanford.edu/entries/science-mechanisms/)
producing them ([Werner 1998](https://academic.oup.com/book/51110/chapter-abstract/421887314)).
Model-building is essential because it lets us expand our view of the study
system and turn ecology into a predictive science.

Other influential papers that shaped our thinking (chronological):
[Brown 1995](http://ifile.it/dpxqf3v/brown__-_macroecology.pdf),
[Lawton 1999](https://www.jstor.org/stable/3546712),
[Hubbell 2001](http://ecologia.ib.usp.br/bie5778/lib/exe/fetch.php?media=hubbell2001.pdf),
[Simberloff 2004](https://www.journals.uchicago.edu/doi/full/10.1086/420777),
[Roughgarden 2009](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10539-009-9164-z),
[Scheiner & Willig 2008](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12080-007-0002-0),
and [Vellend 2010](https://sites.google.com/site/diogoprovetepage/pdf-s/Vellend2010.QRBiol.thetheoryofcommunityecology.PDF).

We strive to make our science as **open as possible**. We always post
preprints to public repositories — there are many advantages, [especially
for early-career researchers](https://journals.plos.org/plosbiology/article?id=10.1371/journal.pbio.3000151),
including [increased citations](https://elifesciences.org/articles/52646).
